nodes.description: TRIP11 encodes GMAP-210, an essential tether protein of the Golgi apparatus. ODCD alleles reduce but do not abolish GMAP-210: a splice variant in trans with a null allele yields a low-abundance but partly functional protein. One recurrent allele, c.586C>T p.(Gln196*), is present in seven individuals from four families across different regions and behaves as a hotspot.

evidence.reference_title: Hypomorphic mutations of TRIP11 cause odontochondrodysplasia.
evidence.snippet: TRIP11 encodes Golgi-associated microtubule-binding protein 210 (GMAP-210), an essential tether protein of the Golgi apparatus that physically interacts with intraflagellar transport 20 (IFT20), a component of the ciliary intraflagellar transport complex B.

evidence.reference_title: Description of four patients with TRIP11 variants expand the clinical spectrum of odontochondroplasia (ODCD) and demonstrate the existence of common variants.
evidence.snippet: The c.586C>T; p.(Gln196*) variant, previously shown by mRNA studies to result in p.Val105_Gln196del, is the most frequent variant, present in seven individuals from four families, three from different regions of the world, suggesting that it may be a variant hotspot.

nodes.description: The functional studies are unusually decisive about compartment: despite GMAP-210's physical interaction with IFT20 and the extraskeletal features that suggested a ciliopathy, patient-derived primary cells support a Golgi-based mechanism. Golgi integrity, global secretion and IFT20 distribution are all preserved; what fails is glycan processing and the secretion of extracellular matrix proteoglycans.
